title: Deterministic Verification and a Single‑Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (exactly one initial generation call per intent; that same candidate reused for both baseline and guarded episodes) we generated one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251. Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. The preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed; the reported confirmatory estimand applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition run. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived and referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps), promising faster authoring of device CLI sequences and intent-driven automation. Stochastic generation, however, creates operational risk: syntax errors, incorrect command ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties can produce unsafe or non-functional device changes. Prior empirical and survey work documents LLM feasibility for draft configurations while highlighting the continuing need for deterministic verification or human oversight [1],[2].

A widely adopted architectural response is to interpose a deterministic validator between generation and acceptance, optionally followed by bounded automated repair — a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pattern — which accepts only validator-passed candidates or attempts limited repair when mechanically verifiable defects are detected [3],[4]. These pipelines demonstrably reduce mechanically verifiable error classes (syntax, simple ordering and local-policy violations), but open questions remain about the marginal benefit of such guardrails when modern LLM outputs already conform to validator encodings under constrained task regimes.

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that isolates the marginal verifier+single-repair effect when the same initial candidate is reused across conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics). By design the experiment measures only the validator-and-repair marginal effect on identical model outputs rather than conflating generation variability across conditions. We executed N_pairs = 250 intents on a synthetic/emulation partition. Our principal contribution is the concrete, artifact-grounded quantification of the marginal verifier-detected improvement (and its statistical bounds) under shared_initial_candidate semantics for a constrained NetOps task set.
sections.related_work:
Surveys and recent NetOps-focused studies establish that (i) LLMs can produce usable draft configurations in controlled setups [1],[2]; (ii) deterministic network verification tools (header-space analysis, Batfish-like engines, model checking) are mature methods for mechanized checks of forwarding, reachability, and many local-policy properties and are commonly used as validators in GVR pipelines [3],[5]; and (iii) generate-and-verify and program-repair workflows increase detection and correction rates for mechanically checkable defects in code and configuration domains, while limitations remain for deeper semantic correctness and cross-vendor subtleties [4],[6].

Security analyses of prompt-injection and retrieval-based threats emphasize the need for filtering and validation layers in LLM-integrated pipelines but note that adaptive adversaries remain an unresolved operational threat [7].

Our study differs from prior reports by (i) using a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics that isolates the validator/repair marginal effect on identical generated candidates, (ii) reporting reconciled provider-call accounting for stage-level mapping of generation and repair events, and (iii) archiving validator traces and reconciliation artifacts so the numeric outcomes and stage mappings are auditable.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 and specified a confirmatory paired design with N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, and primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration froze the single-repair policy, exclusion rules, the analysis tests (exact McNemar two-sided and paired-bootstrap percentile CIs), and the maximum model-call budget. The preregistration artifact SHA-256 is 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics. Under the registered shared_initial_candidate design exactly one initial model-generation call was produced per intent and that same generated candidate was reused for both episodes (baseline and guarded); no independent first-pass generation per condition was performed. This isolates the marginal effect of deterministic validation and the single permitted repair on an identical candidate. Adapter reconciliation recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 251 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}.

Task generation and constraints. A deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced 250 constrained intent tasks. Each task payload encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and a difficulty label (medium/hard/very_hard). Tasks exercised workflow constraints (make-before-break uplink switchover, paired-link atomic MTU changes, safe access transfer patterns) and enforced protected interfaces that must not be modified. The full task manifest is archived as part of the evidence bundle.

Model invocation policy, validator, and repair template. All initial generations used the declared model gpt-5-mini. For each intent we executed one shared initial generation call. The guarded pipeline submitted the shared candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5, which implements full_intent_constraint_validation: parsing CLI sequences, checking required_sequence ordering, validating workflow constraints, and comparing the resulting final_state snapshot to the expected_final_state encoded in the task payload. When the validator returned valid = false the pipeline permitted up to one automated, template-driven repair attempt (deterministic syntactic or ordering fixes) and re-submitted the repaired candidate to the validator. No multi-iteration or human escalation was permitted.

Inclusion and contamination rules. The preregistered exclusion rules removed items failing vendor-parsers that prevented verification or items with credential-like tokens or denylist hits. Contamination detectors flagged instruction-like embedded tokens; flagged items would be excluded from the primary analysis and treated in sensitivity analyses. In this confirmatory run no episodes were excluded or flagged, and the complete_pair_count is 250.

Confirmatory analysis. The preregistered primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1. The primary test is an exact two-sided McNemar on the paired outcomes; we also computed a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for the guarded − baseline paired difference using 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Analysis artifacts (contingency table and condition summary) are archived in the evidence bundle.
sections.results:
Execution and raw counts. Execution completed the preregistered confirmatory partition with planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250, and model_calls_used = 251. Provider-call accounting reconciles to 250 shared initial-generation calls plus 1 repair call.

Primary binary outcomes and contingency. Validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table observed is n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant pair (baseline failed, guarded passed) corresponds to the only exercised repair call; the repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition is 1/250 = 0.4%.

Statistical inference. The exact McNemar two-sided test on discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) returned p = 1.0. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for the guarded − baseline paired difference (10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] in proportion units (i.e., 0 – 1.2 percentage points). These analysis outputs and bootstrap parameters are archived.

Representative validator diagnostics and repairs. Validator traces for passed episodes show parsed_command_count equal to each task's required_command_count. Representative scoring artifacts (examples drawn from execution/scoring entries) show consistent normalization and valid=true across both episodes for the majority of tasks. Only one automated repair call occurred and converted the single failing baseline candidate to a guarded pass; the repair was a constrained ordering/syntactic template and did not introduce new touched interfaces beyond those allowed by the task payload.
sections.discussion:
Operational meaning of the near‑null marginal effect. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation partition used here, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the guarded pipeline converted the lone failing candidate via the single permitted repair. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) provides an empirical bound on the possible verifier-improvement under this pipeline and task scope.

Reasons artifact-grounded. Three artifact-grounded factors explain the small observed guarded gain: (1) the deterministic task generator encoded constrained intents and allowed_touched_fields that reduced task ambiguity and favored well-formed CLI sequences; (2) the declared model (gpt-5-mini) produced highly consistent, syntactically well-formed sequences for these constrained intents; and (3) the deterministic validator checks mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, expected_final_state snapshots) and does not capture broader behavioral correctness in live protocol execution or cross-device emergent interactions.

Power, assumptions, and interpretation. The preregistration power calculation assumed a baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 when selecting N_pairs = 250 to target detection of a 15 percentage-point absolute effect with ≈80% power. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) is substantially higher than assumed and therefore reduces the ability to reject a null of zero paired difference for small absolute improvements. Consequently, the paired-bootstrap confidence interval that bounds the maximum plausible verifier-detected improvement under the study conditions is the most practically informative output.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: results depend on prompt templates, the single-repair policy, shared_initial_candidate semantics, and the precise validator encoding. Construct validity: the deterministic validator measures mechanically verifiable correctness but does not assert live protocol-level correctness. External validity: the confirmatory evidence covers only the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed in this run. Security: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not exercised and remain open threats.

Appropriate operational framing. These results indicate that in tightly constrained emulation-style tasks with a capable LLM the marginal verifier-detected improvement from a single repair may be small. This should not be interpreted to mean validators or repair stages are unnecessary in broader or adversarial operational contexts: (a) validator scope matters — validators that check properties not present here could catch errors not exercised in our task bank; (b) multi-iteration repairs, human escalation, or richer external tests could produce different operational benefits; and (c) production heterogeneity and adversaries may materially change the benefit calculus.

Reproducibility. All run artifacts (raw model responses, execution manifest, validator traces, repair traces, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis outputs) are archived in a single evidence bundle manifest. Key numeric facts reported above (model_calls_used = 251, stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}, contingency counts n11=249/n10=1/n01=0/n00=0, and bootstrap parameters) are reproducible from the archived manifests and analysis CSVs referenced in the Disclosure Statement.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). We explicitly disclose that the preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast was not executed and that the executed confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on the synthetic/emulation partition only. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts referenced in this paper are archived and available in the evidence bundle described in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and performed pre-lock infrastructure development only; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and execution summary: declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Execution used a guarded generate–verify–repair flow permitting at most one automated repair per episode. Confirmatory execution completed planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, and model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial_generation + 1 repair) per the adapter reconciliation in the archived manifest.

Preregistration and immutable prompt reference: preregistration study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). Immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.

Evidence bundle pointer: a single archived evidence-bundle manifest contains the full execution and analysis artifacts (model responses, task manifest, validator traces, repair traces, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis CSVs). The archived bundle is referenced by its manifest within the run artifact set (see the execution manifest included in the archived evidence bundle). That manifest is the authoritative pointer to per-file artifacts and hashes for auditing; per-file paths and full hashes are preserved in the archived bundle rather than reproduced in this statement.

Executed estimand and deviation disclosure: The preregistration included multiple partitions (synthetic/emulation, community, production-like) and a preregistered sim-to-real confirmatory contrast. Deviation disclosure (explicit): the preregistered sim-to-real confirmatory comparison was not executed in this run; the executed confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated on the synthetic/emulation partition only (N_pairs = 250; shared_initial_candidate semantics).
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax and prescribed workflow sequences) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, emergent interactions).
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
